title: API Versioning
body:
Keeping an old [[API]] contract working while a new one rolls out — the old menu stays available for regulars. Usually expressed in the path (`/v1/reviews`, `/v2/reviews`), sometimes in a header or a query parameter. Both versions are maintained on the server, often routing into shared business logic with different serialisation on top.

The reason it exists: once third parties integrate against your contract, you cannot unilaterally break it. A frontend you control can be redeployed in an afternoon; a client's integration cannot. Versioning is the mechanism for making a breaking change without breaking anyone — you ship v2, migrate consumers over time, then deprecate v1 with notice.
